description: Add rows to the end of the visual's data and drop the oldest past keepLast; the visual's settings are unchanged. Adds rows to a bar, bar-horizontal, line, area, table or scatter visual; its settings (xKey, series, columns) are unchanged, and numeric strings are coerced as on push. On a map visual the rows merge by region code: a row whose region code matches a stored row replaces it, the others are added, and keepLast is ignored. On a progress visual the rows merge by name: a row whose name matches a stored row replaces it, the others are added, and keepLast is ignored. On a status-grid visual the rows merge by name: a row whose name matches a stored row replaces it, the others are added, and keepLast is ignored. On a heatmap visual the rows merge by cell (x and y) or date: a row whose cell (x and y) or date matches a stored row replaces it, the others are added, and keepLast is ignored. On these an append that would make more rows than the type's cap is refused at rows; replace the whole list with PUT /v1/visuals/{id}/data instead. A calendar layout keeps its latest 366 days: the latest date sets the 366-day window, older days, stored or sent, are dropped and counted in dropped, and an append that would push every stored day out of it is refused, so a mistyped year cannot erase the calendar. A pie, kpi, markdown, funnel or gauge visual has no row list: replace its document with PUT /v1/visuals/{id}/data instead. Over HTTP keepLast may also go in the query string (?keepLast=7), and the body may be text/csv: the header row is the keys the visual's rows have. Needs an API key: with none yet, call signup first.

keepLast.description: Keep only the newest keepLast rows after the append, dropping the oldest. The type's cap applies in any case: line 500, area 500, bar 500, bar-horizontal 500, scatter 500, table 200, map 4000, progress 20, status-grid 200, heatmap 1000 rows.

rows.description: Added after the rows the visual holds, in order.

items.description: One data row, with the keys the visual's rows have: the xKey and the series keys, or the column keys.
